messages:
anya: quick heads-up — celeste-v1 int4 canary finished on dedicated pool and we see a structured-output compliance regression for funcalls. baseline (fp16) =~0.9% parse failures, celeste int4 = 3.8%
anya: failure mode looks correlated with KV-cache batching and requests that contain long system prompts
anya: sample log snippet: ```
INFER [req=2048] model=celeste-v1-int4 batch=24 kvcache=true prompt_len=820 output="{\"action\": \"create_ticket\", \"fields\": [ ...\" "
>> parse error at offset 243: unexpected '\\n'
```
tom: ouch. is this only when batch>1?
anya: yes, single-shot mirrored requests on same model looked fine in local replay. batch>=8 shows the spike.
jun: could be token boundary reorder or partial-kv read when quant kernels fuse attention — i've seen similar in older int4 boots
eva: @jun any quick diagnostic to prove it's kvcache vs tokenizer? can we toggle kv off in the canary?
jun: we can flip runtime flag mirror_kv=false for a short run. also request to log last N tokens emitted before end-of-output for failing calls
anya: did a short run with mirror_kv=false — failure rate dropped to 1.1% (500 sample run)
anya: deploy-bot: Canary run summary: total=2000, pass=96.2%, fail=3.8%, model=celeste-v1-int4, config=dedicated-gpu-kv-enabled
anya: proposed mitigations: 1) enable quick preflight JSON shim (wrap expected funcall payload in guarded envelope to reduce newline/escape fragility), 2) increase retry budget for funcalls from 2 -> 4 for int4 canaries, 3) temporary autoswitch: prefer mirror replica without kv for canary traffic while we root cause
tom: preflight JSON shim example?
anya: quick prototype snippet: ```json
{"__preflight": true, "payload": "<original prompt here>"}
```
anya: shim unwrap happens in postprocess step before parse attempt; if parse fails, we run JSON-repair heuristics + retry
eva: for retries we should ensure idempotency markers so downstream tool calls aren’t duplicated. add header X-funcall-id and dedupe at tool-router
jun: agree. also will run low-level debug with kv read offsets enabled to see if fused kernels truncate tail tokens under batching
tom: timeline? can we test mirror_kv=false run at scale and toggle retry budget tonight?
anja: (typo) I meant anya :P
anya: plan — run a 10k sample with mirror_kv=false tomorrow morning, enable shim and retry budget change in canary only, collect structured-output metrics and token trace. tagging @tom @jun to coordinate.
eva: SGTM. I'll add an entry to the canary playbook and the console dashboard so we can track parse failure metric by batch size
jun: if kv read offsets show mismatch i'll open a low-priority kernel ticket. may need a micro-quant recompile path for certain attention kernels
tom: thanks. small ask: capture a few full raw traces for 5 failing calls (with inputs) so we can run offline repair heuristics
anya: will attach those to the canary ticket. thanks team :thumbsup:
